original_question: In the theory of Chebyshev functions and Klee functions for a proper lower semicontinuous function g: X -> [-infinity, +infinity], the paper uses the halved Euclidean distance q = (1/2)||.||^2 through the proximal map P_lambda g and the farthest map Q_mu g. What are the corresponding characterizations when the Euclidean discrepancy is replaced by a Bregman distance generated by a Legendre function f? In particular, how should one characterize the admissible generator f and the analogue of the Chebyshev point in that Bregman setting?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 7, read in light of Section 7 (Definition 7.4, Fact 7.5, Fact 7.7, Definition 7.9, Theorem 7.10): the open problem asking for Bregman-distance analogues of the Euclidean characterizations for Chebyshev/Klee functions and for the μ-Chebyshev point of a function g. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies that the paper is asking for a Bregman-distance replacement of the Euclidean Section 7 theory, and it correctly points to the proximal map P_λg, the farthest map Q_μg, the role of a Legendre generator, and the analogue of the Chebyshev point. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
missing_details: The paper’s exact target is not a general classification of “admissible generators” f; rather, it asks for Bregman-distance analogues of the specific Euclidean Section 7 objects and results. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
Section 7 works in the finite-dimensional Euclidean setting X = ℝ^n and assumes g: X → [-∞,+∞] is proper and lower semicontinuous. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
The exact Euclidean objects to be generalized are the envelopes and maps e_λg, P_λg, φ_μg, and Q_μg, not only the maps themselves. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))

The relevant parameter ranges are part of the statement: λ must satisfy 0 < λ < λ_g, and μ must satisfy μ > μ_g, where λ_g and μ_g are the thresholds introduced in Definition 7.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))

The Euclidean characterization being generalized is the equivalence between differentiability of e_λg or φ_μg, single-valuedness of P_λg or Q_μg, and essential strict convexity of g + λ^{-1}q or g - μ^{-1}q. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The Chebyshev-point part refers specifically to the μ-Chebyshev point p_μ ∈ argmin φ_μg, which Theorem 7.10 characterizes by p_μ ∈ conv Q_μg(p_μ). ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))

The open problem explicitly concerns both the Chebyshev-function side and the Klee-function side; your draft under-specifies the Klee-envelope/farthest-map half of the problem. ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let X = ℝ^n, let g: X → [-∞,+∞] be proper and lower semicontinuous, and let q(x) = (1/2)‖x‖^2. For 0 < λ < λ_g and μ > μ_g, Section 7 defines the Euclidean Moreau/Klee envelopes and maps by e_λg(x) = inf_w [g(w) + λ^{-1}q(x-w)], P_λg(x) = argmin_w [g(w) + λ^{-1}q(x-w)], φ_μg(y) = sup_x [μ^{-1}q(y-x) - g(x)], and Q_μg(y) = argmax_x [μ^{-1}q(y-x) - g(x)], and proves that single-valuedness of P_λg and Q_μg is equivalent to differentiability of e_λg and φ_μg and to essential strict convexity of g + λ^{-1}q and g - μ^{-1}q; it also proves that the μ-Chebyshev point p_μ, defined as the unique minimizer of φ_μg, is characterized by p_μ ∈ conv Q_μg(p_μ). What are the exact analogues of these results when the halved Euclidean distance q is replaced by a Bregman distance D_f generated by a Legendre function f on ℝ^n; that is, how should one formulate and characterize the Bregman versions of the λ-Chebyshev function, the μ-Klee function, the associated envelope/proximal/farthest constructions, and the Chebyshev point of g? ([citeseerx.ist.psu.edu](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=bc7bfc1f3fe86b66e48fce0a9522c5dd560c873b&repid=rep1&type=pdf&utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft unmistakably targets Section 7/Problem 7 rather than an earlier part of the chapter, because it names the Euclidean discrepancy q = (1/2)‖·‖^2, the proximal map P_λg, the farthest map Q_μg, and the Chebyshev point—exactly the objects introduced and analyzed in Section 7, and then turned into an open Bregman-distance question in Problem 7. The paper’s nearby context shows that the intended Euclidean benchmarks are Fact 7.5, Fact 7.7, and Theorem 7.10, and Problem 7 asks for their Bregman-distance counterparts, not for a broader or different generalization. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1003.3127))
